subject: Proportions for TV units and feature walls
hook: Most media walls that look 'off' have a proportion problem, not a style problem.
ig:
Most media walls that look 'off' have a proportion problem, not a style problem.

Before anyone picks a finish, these are the numbers worth knowing:

1. Your seated eye height. Sit where you actually watch and measure floor to eye. The centre of the screen should sit near that line, not halfway up the wall.
2. The margin around the TV. A recess that fits the screen exactly looks cramped. Leave space either side, and think about the next TV you'll buy.
3. Thirds, not halves. A long, low base with lighter shelving above usually looks calmer than a wall split straight down the middle.
4. The chimney breast and alcoves. Matching units either side keep the wall balanced, even when the alcoves aren't quite identical.
5. Depth versus walkway. Enough room for a soundbar and console, but not so deep it eats into your route across the room.

A bespoke media wall is designed around these measurements, which is why we start with a survey, not a catalogue.

Save this for when you measure up, then book a free, no-obligation design consultation through the link in bio.

Ever sat down in front of a new TV wall and felt something wasn't quite right? Nine times out of ten it's the proportions.

Our quick guide covers the five things we check on every media wall survey: seated eye height, the margin around the screen, splitting the wall in thirds, working with your chimney breast and alcoves, and how deep the base can go before it gets in the way.

Grab a tape measure this week, jot your numbers down, and bring them along to a free, no-obligation design consultation. We'll design the wall around your room rather than the other way round.

on_asset:
S1: Why some media walls look 'off' / Six proportion rules to check first |
S2: Screen at seated eye height — Sit on your own sofa and measure to your eye line. The middle of the screen should sit close to that, not in the middle of the wall. |
S3: Give the screen breathing room — A panel or recess only just wider than the TV looks squeezed. Leave a margin, and allow for the next size of TV you might buy. |
S4: Think in thirds, not halves — A low, long base and lighter shelving above usually reads better than a wall split evenly top and bottom. |
S5: Let the chimney breast lead — If you have alcoves, size the units to them and keep both sides matching so the wall feels balanced, even if the alcoves differ slightly. |
S6: Depth that suits the walkway — Deep enough for a soundbar, console and router, shallow enough that nobody clips it walking past. Measure your route through the room. |
S7: Save this before your survey — Eye height, margin, thirds, alcoves, depth. Bring the numbers to a free design consultation. Link in bio. |
